lead: Durham has grown fast, and most of its homes are newer. But humid summers, crawl spaces and heavy Piedmont storms still bring a steady flow of leaks and wet floors.
risk: crawl space moisture, storm leaks and creek flooding
why: Many Durham homes, old and new, sit over a crawl space instead of a slab or basement. In a humid North Carolina summer, that space can stay damp for months. A leaking supply line or a loose duct joint adds even more water. Floor joists swell, insulation sags and mold starts on the wood. Owners often notice a musty smell or a soft spot in the floor before they see any water.

Big storms are the other risk. Hurricane Fran in 1996 dropped heavy rain and brought down trees across the Triangle, and strong summer storms still do the same on a smaller scale. Ellerbe Creek and Third Fork Creek can rise fast when rain falls hard on paved ground. Homes in low areas near those creeks see water in yards, crawl spaces and finished lower floors.

image_caption: In Durham, a slow leak often shows up first as a stain on the ceiling or a soft floor.
problems: Older homes in Walltown, Old West Durham
Crawl space drying and mold control
Wooded areas like Hope Valley, Forest Hills
Low areas near Ellerbe and Third Fork creeks
tips: Check the crawl space after big storms and in late summer.
Keep gutters and downspouts sending water well away from the house.
Trim large limbs that hang over the roof before storm season.
Replace rubber washing machine hoses with braided steel.
areas: Calls come from Downtown, Trinity Park, Walltown, Old West Durham, Forest Hills, Hope Valley, Woodcroft and Brightleaf, plus Chapel Hill, Morrisville and Research Triangle Park.

faq.q: Why does my Durham crawl space smell musty?
faq.a: A musty smell usually means moisture and early mold. In Durham, humid air, poor drainage or a slow plumbing leak can keep a crawl space wet. DryFlare finds the source, dries the wood and can treat mold. A vapor barrier and good drainage help keep it dry after that.
